title: Eric Wentz
text:
About Me
I’m Eric Wentz, a junior at Macalester College, majoring in Data Science with a minor in Computer Science. I have a deep passion for sports analytics, combining my experience as a collegiate basketball player with my technical expertise in data science, machine learning, and predictive modeling.
I have worked on NBA, NFL, and MLB data projects, developing statistical models, visualizations, and AI-driven insights. My experience includes internships with ShotCaller, where I engineered data pipelines and built interactive dashboards, and SponsorUnited, where I tracked sponsorship activations at live sporting events. Additionally, I gained event operations experience with the Minnesota Vikings, managing logistics for gamedays, training camp, and premium events.
As a team captain for Macalester Men’s Basketball and a former practice player for the WNBA’s Minnesota Lynx, I bring a unique perspective to sports analytics—understanding both the data and the game itself. My goal is to leverage data-driven insights to enhance athlete performance, team strategy, and fan engagement in professional sports.
Education
Macalester College, St. Paul, MN (2022 – 2026)
Major: Data Science | Minor: Computer Science GPA: 3.71/4.00 Relevant Coursework: Machine Learning, Data Science, Statistical Modeling, Linear Algebra, Programming (Python, R, Java), Git/GitHub Leadership: Team Captain – Macalester Men’s Basketball, SAAC Board Member (1 of 7 selected from 400+ athletes) New York University – Tisch Institute for Global Sport
Completed coursework in Sports Management, Data Analytics, Marketing, and Technology in Sports Gained insights into the business and data-driven aspects of professional sports

title: QB Visuals
text:
This project uses Next Gen Stats, Pro Football Reference, and ESPN QBR data to generate percentile-based visualizations of NFL quarterbacks.

Project Highlights

Data Sources: Next Gen Stats, Pro Football Reference, ESPN QBR.
Key Insights: QB playstyle, efficiency, and advanced metrics.
Tools Used: ggplot2, tidyverse, dplyr, grid, png.



Methodology
The project processes quarterback data by: 1. Loading Next Gen Stats, Advanced Stats, and QBR Data. 2. Filtering & Cleaning Data (e.g., removing duplicates, ensuring completeness). 3. title: NBA Interactive Player Comparison App
text:
This project presents an interactive NBA player comparison app, allowing users to evaluate basketball skills, compare their attributes to NBA players, and create hypothetical player profiles using percentile-based metrics.

Project Highlights

Data Sources: Player statistics from the NBA database.
Key Features:

Compare your skills to real NBA players.
Find the top 3 most similar NBA players to a given set of attributes.
Generate custom radar charts to visualize player profiles.
Explore an interactive scatter plot mapping player styles.

Tools Used: shiny, ggplot2, plotly, dplyr, DT.




🔹 Features & Methodology

🏀 Player Skill Comparison

Users input their own basketball attributes (shooting, passing, defense, rebounding, scoring).
The app compares these attributes to a dataset of NBA players.
Displays the top 3 closest players based on Euclidean distance.



📊 Radar Charts for Visual Representation

Radar charts visualize how a user or NBA player ranks across 5 key basketball skills.
The app calculates the area of the radar chart to measure similarity.
Users can compare their radar chart side-by-side with real NBA players.



📈 Interactive Scatter Plot (MDS)

Displays NBA player clusters based on similarity.
Users can see where their custom or hypothetical player falls among real NBA players.



🔮 Hypothetical Player Builder

Users input percentile values for each skill.
The app converts percentiles into real NBA statistics.
Custom player profiles are generated and saved for future comparisons.

title: The Evolution of the Three-Point Shot in the NBA
text:
This project presents an in-depth statistical analysis of how the three-point shot has evolved in the NBA, influencing player salaries, positional play, and team success over time.

Project Highlights

Data Sources: NBA player statistics and salaries from Kaggle and GitHub.
Key Research Areas:

How three-point attempts have changed across different player positions.
The relationship between three-point attempts and player salaries.
The correlation between three-point shooting efficiency and team wins.

Tools Used: R, ggplot2, dplyr, regression modeling.




🔹 Research Questions & Methodology

🏀 Evolution of Three-Point Attempts by Position

Compared three-point attempts for guards, forwards, and centers between 2010 and 2020.
Results indicate a significant increase in three-point attempts across all positions.



💰 Impact on Player Salaries

2010 vs. 2020: Examined the top 50 highest-paid players in each year.
Regression analysis shows that three-point attempts were undervalued in 2010 but had a strong positive correlation with salary in 2020.



📊 Correlation Between Three-Point Shooting & Team Success

Analyzed whether paying for elite three-point shooters leads to more wins.
Found a positive correlation but suggests diminishing returns—teams should balance spending across multiple skill sets.





📈 Key Findings

The NBA has shifted toward a three-point-heavy game.
Higher-paid players now take more threes, unlike in 2010.
While three-point efficiency contributes to team success, teams must still diversify their strategies.

🚀 Future Research Directions

Should the NBA introduce a four-point line?
Are three-pointers overvalued, or should teams invest even more in shooters?
How has team strategy evolved beyond the three-pointer?

title: New York Red Bulls Match Analysis
text:
This project provides a detailed match analysis of the New York Red Bulls, using advanced soccer metrics and visualizations.

Project Highlights

Data Sources: MLS Stats, Wyscout, Opta.
Key Insights: Passing networks, xG analysis, defensive structures, and key match trends.
Tools Used: ggplot2, tidyverse, dplyr, gganimate, ggridges.



Methodology
This analysis focuses on: 1. Passing Trends & Efficiency → Examining completed vs. incomplete passes by zone. 2. Expected Goals (xG) Analysis → Evaluating shot quality & efficiency. 3. Defensive Performance → Analyzing opponent shot selection & defensive structure. 4. Possession Breakdown → Comparing time of possession and playing style.



📊 Key Match Insights

🔹 Passing Breakdown

The defending third had the highest number of incomplete passes despite having the fewest pass attempts.
10% of passes in the defending third were incomplete, compared to 6% in the attacking third and 3.9% in the middle third.
67% of turnovers were unforced, highlighting a lack of ball security.



🔹 xG & Shooting Analysis

The Red Bulls generated 1.797 expected goals (xG), outperforming the MLS league average of 1.347.
47% of shots came from outside the box, in line with the MLS average, but the Red Bulls were far more efficient from distance.
19-yard goal in the second minute → Showed confidence in long-range shooting.



🔹 Defensive Effectiveness

Opposing offense managed just 7 total shots and only 2 on target.
Average shot distance conceded: 21.76 yards → No clean looks in the penalty area.



🔹 Possession & Playing Style

Opposition controlled the ball for nearly 14 more minutes despite losing 4-0.
Red Bulls’ “run and gun” style led to quick turnovers but high shot volume.
Early goal in the second minute likely influenced their high-risk, high-reward approach.





📽 Interactive Slideshow
To explore dynamic passing networks, shot maps, and possession trends, check out the interactive slideshow below:



NY Red Bulls Match Slideshow


👆 Click the image to view the full match analysis slideshow.



Final Thoughts
The New York Red Bulls’ approach revolves around: ✅ Fast-paced attacking play → Prioritizing shot volume over possession.
✅ Aggressive shooting from distance → More effective than MLS averages.
✅ Defensive pressure forcing low-quality shots → Limiting opponent efficiency.
This high-energy, counter-attacking style secured a 4-0 victory despite having significantly less possession.

title: A Decade of Athletic Spending: Trends, Disparities, and Impact on Success
text:
This project presents an in-depth analysis of university athletic spending, exploring trends, disparities, and potential correlations with team success over the past decade. The study leverages publicly available data to evaluate the financial landscape of collegiate sports.

📊 Project Highlights

Data Sources:

U.S. Department of Education University and College Athletic Expenditure Reports

Ethics in Athletic Disclosure Act

Federally funded co-ed schools


Key Areas of Focus:

Budget trends across institutions
Athletic spending patterns
Comparative analysis of basketball teams
The relationship between spending and success


Tools Used: R, ggplot2, dplyr, Shiny, Data Visualization




🔹 Key Findings & Methodology

📈 University Athletic Spending Trends

Analysis of overall school budget changes over time.
Athletic department budgets compared across institutions.
Identifying disparities in spending between schools.



🏀 Basketball Team Comparison

Comparative study of athletic investment in basketball programs.
Evaluating participant spending and its influence on team performance.
Measuring the financial gap between successful and struggling programs.



📉 Impact on Success

Investigating whether increased spending correlates with better athletic performance.
Addressing limitations in data:

Excludes donations and external funding sources.
Does not adjust for inflation.
Finding little correlation between spending and success.
